findings.title: corrective coordination
findings.claim: The coordinating wa joins the prohibition of one gate to the positive alternative of entering through separated gates.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the conjunction before the second entry clause; its trigger is the immediately preceding prohibited route, so the two clauses read as one correction rather than unrelated instructions.
findings.reader_payoff: The route advice becomes a single before-and-after instruction: block concentration, then prescribe dispersion.
findings.containment: This records clause linkage only; it does not infer a wider discourse function.

epistemic.reason: The local coordinator is explicitly supplied as the link between the negative and positive route clauses.

findings.title: positive entry command
findings.claim: The second entry clause commands the same sons to enter, so the prohibition limits route configuration rather than entry itself.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the imperative entry verb; the trigger is its shared root and addressee pattern with the earlier jussive prohibition, and their contact reverses the polarity while preserving the action.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish forbidden concentration from permitted movement.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the local command pair and does not claim that every later entry scene is part of this syntax.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies a trusted imperative sharing the entry root and plural addressees with the prohibition.

findings.title: plural-route preposition
findings.claim: The second min binds the positive command to multiple gates and makes the correction parallel to the first route phrase.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the preposition governing the plural gate noun; the trigger is the earlier identical route preposition governing the singular gate, and the parallel construction makes number carry the tactical contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The shift from one route to several is heard in matched grammar, not only inferred from the nouns.
findings.containment: This is a local route-frame effect, not a general metaphysical meaning of the preposition.

epistemic.reason: The repeated preposition is directly tied to the plural gate phrase and parallels the first route phrase.
